To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel, low-cost, multiple-antenna, noncoherent, data-aided UWB-IR synchronizer, which achieves the CRB and is capable of operating under both acquisition and tracking conditions, while it is fully independent of the unknown number of paths comprising a multiple-antenna multipath fading channel.

the proposed synchronizer achieves the CRB for the joint estimate of the arrival times of multiple-antennas affected multipath fading channels without any a priori information on the channel gain amplitudes, and that the performance gain arising from the use of multiple antennas is significant.

(i) the multiple-antennas paradigm can be effectively exploited in order to achieve accurate noncoherent synchronization of UWB-IP signals over broadband channels affected by multipath, (ii) the number of antennas required for achieving the CRB can be significantly lower than that required by the conventional single-antenna approach (e.g., the CRB is achievable with only one antenna), and (iii) a low-cost analog front-end implementation of the proposed ML synchronizer can be achieved
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ML noncoherent data aided joint estimation of the number of multipath components and their arrival times for UWB-IR terminals that employ multiple antennas.
the noncoherent synchronization of UWB- IR signals that are transmitted over multiple-antenna broadband channels, and affected by multipath propagation.
the ML noncoherent data aided joint synchronization of multiple- antenna UWB-IR channels that are affected by multipaths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed synchronizer provides a low-cost and robust solution for the noncoherent data-aide synchronization of UWB-IPR multiple-antenna multipath channels.

the proposed synchronizer achieves a near-optimum performance (in terms of both the number of paths estimate and the accuracy of the corresponding time-delays estimates) for a very low implementation complexity.
the proposed synchronizer provides a low-complexity and robust solution to the noncoherent synchronization problem of multipath-impacted UWB-IR systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an ML noncoherent synchronizer that can be used for the synchronization of multipath-impacted multiple-antenna UWB-IR terminals.

the developed noncoherent ML synchronizer achieves the CRB, and its performance gain arising from the use of multiple antennas is fully independent from both the number of multipath components and their fading statistics.

, for the first time, a ML noncoherent data-aide synchronizer is proposed for multiple-antenna UWB-IR terminals that operates over broadband channels with a priori (e.g., unknown) number of paths and statistics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multiple-antenna UWB-IR systems can benefit from a low-complexity ML noncoherent synchronization technique with performance approaching the CRB.

the ML data- aided synchronization of UWB- IR signals can be performed with high accuracy, without requiring any a posteriori estimate or any a priori information of the channel parameters, by exploiting the multiple-antennas paradigm and by employing a bank of sliding- window correlators.

the exploitation of multiple antennas in conjunction with the proposed ML noncoherent data-aids synchronization algorithm is a promising solution for the accurate and efficient acquisition and tracking of UWB- IR signals over broadband multipath channels.
